example_input: A person drags a card into In Progress. The executor creates the card's worktree and gVisor sandbox, runs the model loop against a local llama.cpp endpoint, answers one question the model asks, and lands the card in Review - where the person reads the diff and clicks Commit and move to done.
note: Every module link pins the exact tag this teardown is based on - SoftwareRenderer/MIKE @ v0.1.0 (382ec61b).

modules.label: the four columns: backlog, in_progress, review, done
HandleMove: leaving In Progress stops the executor; entering it starts one

steps.narrative: The board has four columns and the column is not decoration. Dragging the card into In Progress calls HandleMove, which starts the executor under the subtask schedule; dragging it back out would stop the run. A card whose children are unfinished does not run its own turn - the schedule starts a child instead.
steps.title: A drag starts the run

modules.label: CreateWorktree: one worktree and branch per task

steps.narrative: StartTask loads the task and project rows, pins the baseline (the base ref and its commit at start), and makes sure the task's worktree exists. The worktree is a host directory; everything the run produces will be host files from the moment they are written.
steps.representation:
task row + project row
  base_ref / base_commit pinned at start
  worktree: .worktrees/<task> on its own branch
steps.title: Baseline pinned, worktree ready

modules.label: executeTask: slot, memory gate, sandbox, then the loop

steps.narrative: Before any container exists, the run takes the per-provider running-task slot and then a memory-gate reservation - in that order, so a queued task holds no sandbox while it waits. The gate admits against a host-wide budget, by default 90 percent of installed RAM.
steps.representation:
acquireTaskSlot(provider) -> acquireMemSlot(budget)
  queued tasks hold no container
  agent providers skip the provider slot
steps.title: Two gates before any container

modules.label: Create: the mounts, the network flag, the memory cap

steps.narrative: One container per task, kanban-sandbox-<taskID>, created through rootless Podman with the runsc runtime. The worktree mounts read-write at /home/sandbox/<project>, its .git pointer file is pinned read-only over it, and the project's .git mounts read-only at its own path. A container that cannot establish the pin is refused. If the project enabled network isolation, the create adds --network none.
steps.representation:
podman create --runtime runsc --cap-drop ALL
  --security-opt no-new-privileges --pull never
  -v <worktree>:/home/sandbox/<project>:rw
  -v <worktree>/.git:<mount>/.git:ro   (the pin)
  -v <project>/.git:<project>/.git:ro
steps.title: The sandbox is created

modules.label: the base template: tools, skills, current task, project instructions

steps.narrative: The conversation is rebuilt from stored rows, not kept in a process: groupTaskMessages reassembles assistant rows, tool calls and results, and the system prompt goes in front - tool list, skills, the latest summary, the project's AGENTS.md inside <instructions>, the date, and the working directory (the container mount path when sandboxed).
steps.representation:
system: base.tmpl (tools, skills, summary,
  <instructions> project AGENTS.md, date, cwd)
+ conversation rebuilt from SQLite rows
steps.title: The prompt is a rebuild

modules.label: LlamaClient: communication with llama.cpp OpenAI-compatible API
finalizeTurn settles the turn once the stream ends

steps.narrative: The loop streams one chat completion from the provider - here a local llama.cpp, but any OpenAI-compatible endpoint answers the same shape. Tool-call deltas are folded as they arrive. When the stream ends, finalizeTurn persists the assistant row, then each tool-call row, before anything runs.
steps.representation:
POST <provider>/chat/completions (streaming)
  deltas -> text, reasoning, tool calls
  persist assistant row, then tool_call rows
steps.title: One streaming call, then persist first

modules.label: the 13 core tool names the dispatch and the definitions share

steps.narrative: File, shell and LSP calls cross into the container over the sandbox bridge - one stdio connection, no listener, no port. A sandboxed task whose bridge is missing gets a refusal from every host tool, never a silent host fallback. Results are captured under a byte cap and folded into the next call. The loop repeats with no iteration cap.
steps.representation:
read_file / write_file / edit_file / bash / lsp_*
  -> podman exec -i ... /sandbox-bridge (stdio)
  results capped, persisted, folded in
steps.title: Tools cross the bridge

modules.label: an unanswered question stops the executor and waits
HandleCommitAndDone: the click that commits and merges

steps.narrative: When the model calls ask_question, the executor stops and the card waits in Review until the person answers. When it calls request_review, the card lands in Review with the whole record - conversation, tool calls, diff - and waits there unless the card's auto-commit/auto-merge flags say otherwise. The person reads the diff and clicks Commit and move to done; only staged changes are committed, and Done is set only when the merge reaches the target branch.
steps.representation:
ask_question -> Review, executor exits, wait
request_review -> Review with the full record
a person's click -> commit staged -> merge -> Done
steps.title: The card waits in Review

title: One card, end to end - MIKE
